query: For multicomponent high-entropy alloys in solid and liquid states at and near their high melting temperatures, what single testable methodological intervention could overcome the inability of EAM references to represent the many atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid? Explain why it should improve reference–target phase-space overlap, predict the reduction in thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references, define the applicable composition and temperature ranges, identify supporting evidence from elemental or binary calculations, and specify a decisive free-energy benchmark that would falsify the hypothesis.

generation.hypothesis: Replacing standard embedded-atom (EAM) references with a machine-learning-trained many-body potential, specifically fitted to high-temperature ab initio liquid configurations, will substantially improve reference–target overlap and reduce the thermodynamic-integration path mismatch for multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures (relative to TOR-TILD’s EAM references).
generation.material_initial_state: Multicomponent high-entropy alloys (≥5 principal metallic elements in near-equiatomic ratios) in both solid and liquid states close to their high melting temperatures (≥0.9 Tm).
generation.intervention: Adopt a new reference potential built by training on ab initio molecular dynamics data sampled from the near-melt liquid and high-temperature solid phases, replacing the classical EAM reference in free-energy methods such as TOR-TILD.
generation.conditions: Temperatures from slightly below to slightly above each alloy’s melting point and for compositions spanning equiatomic or near-equiatomic ranges of 3d transition-metal HEAs.
generation.structural_mediator: The advanced many-body potential, which more flexibly captures local atomic environments in both the liquid and high-temperature solid phases.
generation.mechanism: A machine-learning-based many-body reference, trained to accurately reproduce ab initio forces and energies in relevant near-melt configurations, will sample a broader range of local coordination environments than conventional EAM, leading to improved overlap and smaller systematic errors in thermodynamic integration paths.
generation.predicted_outcome: Relative to a classical EAM reference, the new reference potential will yield significantly lower free-energy path integration discrepancies (e.g., by at least a factor of two) for solid–liquid transitions of multicomponent high-entropy alloys near their melting temperatures.
generation.baseline: Existing free-energy calculations with EAM references in TOR-TILD for high-temperature, multicomponent liquids, which often fail to capture the diversity of local atomic environments and suffer from path integration mismatch.
generation.boundary: The approach assumes sufficient high-quality ab initio data to train the reference potential across a range of compositions and temperatures near melting. The method is most directly applicable to 3d transition-metal-based HEAs with stable (or metastable) solid and liquid phases near the targeted temperature regime.
generation.uncertainty: If the fitted model fails to generalize beyond its training data or omits crucial atomic interactions at high temperature, the improved reference–target overlap may not materialize, limiting the reduction of thermodynamic-integration path errors.

falsification_experiment.design: Perform thermodynamic-integration free-energy calculations for a set of equiatomic and near-equiatomic high-entropy alloys using both (i) the newly trained many-body reference potential and (ii) a conventional EAM reference potential, each bridged to the same ab initio target. Compare the free energies and path-integration discrepancies in going from the classical reference to the ab initio potential.
measurements: Free-energy differences between the new many-body reference and the ab initio target at multiple points along the thermodynamic-integration path.
Equivalent differences for an established EAM reference to the same ab initio target.
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the many-body reference potential does not produce significantly lower path-integration discrepancies than EAM (e.g., failing to improve the discrepancy by at least a factor of two), or if it does not remain valid across different HEA compositions and temperatures in the target range, the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text: High strength and ductility, often mutually exclusive properties of a structural material, are also responsible for damage tolerance. At low temperatures, due to high surface energy, single element metallic nanowires such as Ag usually transform into a more preferred phase via nucleation and propagation of partial dislocation through the nanowire, enabling superplasticity. In high entropy alloy (HEA) CoNiCrFeMn nanowires, the motion of the partial dislocation is hindered by the friction due to difference in the lattice parameter of the constituent atoms which is responsible for the hardening and lowering the ductility. In this study, we have examined the temperature-dependent superplasticity of single component Ag and multicomponent CoNiCrFeMn HEA nanowires using molecular dynamics simulations. The results demonstrate that Ag nanowires exhibit apparent temperature-dependent superplasticity at cryogenic temperature due to (110) to (100) cross-section reorientation behavior. Interestingly, HEA nanowires can perform exceptional strength-ductility trade-offs at cryogenic temperatures. chosen.why: By replacing the EAM reference with a more flexible potential trained on high-temperature ab initio data for liquids and solids, the new reference can directly sample a wider range of atomic neighborhoods. This improves the overlap between the reference and ab initio phase spaces, reduces path mismatch in thermodynamic-integration methods, and extends the method’s validity to the relevant composition and temperature regimes.
